subject: Feature-flag contingency & docs owners
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <pm@atlascorp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Feature-flag contingency & docs owners

Team — quick heads-up after the morning sync: two blockers surfaced that need fast cross-functional alignment before we flip the runtime2 feature flag for Atlas integration. I want us to lock the contingency/rollback play and assign a single docs steward so enablement has a canonical source of truth.

Summary (short):
- Risk: We don’t have an agreed rollback/variant-fallback validated end-to-end. If the new runtime behaves unexpectedly under Atlas traffic patterns, we must stop / failover quickly.
- Docs: Enablement and SRE still need the step-by-step runbook and the operator checklist finalized.

Asks (owners + timeline):
- Ben: confirm the technical rollback steps and the exact fallback model id we will route to, and verify we can flip at high velocity. Target: today EOD for the play.
- Laura: own the enablement docs (operator runbook + customer-facing KB). Please scope what you need to finalize it. Target: first draft by Monday EOD.
- Karthik: define the gating metrics (error rate / latency / token-quality signals) for automated aborts.

Proposed mitigation: 5% canary for 24 hours -> health check -> 25% -> 100% with a manual hold at each stage. If Atlas requires tighter constraints, we’ll follow their limit.

Attachments: uv_ready_checklist.xlsx (operator checklist), feature-flag-matrix.csv (matrix of flag states and variant mappings).

I’ll coordinate a brief war-room if we need to cut a hotfix. Please reply with explicit confirmation or blockers.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Launches
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <pm@atlascorp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature-flag contingency & docs owners

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Agree on the canary approach, small clarifications below.

Technical rollback (short):
- Flag is served by config-service /flags/runtime2. We can flip to `runtime-v1-variant` (model variant id: redwood-runtime-v1) instantly; routing is atomic for new connections; in-flight token streams will continue but the KV cache will be rebuilt for new sessions.
- I’ll validate a scripted rollback path (curl + health-check) and a UI switch for emergency ops. Expect a 2-hour smoke/verification window after a rollback to confirm no stale states.

Questions:
- Canary percent? I can do 5% -> 20% -> 100% fully automated with manual gates at 20% and 100%.
- Do we want an immediate auto-abort on latency spikes > 2x p90 or on token-quality regressions (as measured by the QA probe)?

Action: I’ll attach a small runbook snippet into the feature-flag-matrix.csv and push a tested rollback script to the ops repo by EOD.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature-flag contingency & docs owners

Hi Marissa / all — thanks for the proactive heads-up. A couple of constraints from our side that will shape the plan: 

- Legal/compliance: our internal legal team requires us to limit traffic to external vendors at 10% max without an in-market legal attestation. 5% is fine; anything above will add a 48–72 hour delay.
- Observability: we need the replay window enabled so we can validate request/response pairs for the first 24 hours (this is non-negotiable for our PM and SRE leads).
- Customer support: Can we make the rollback path visible to our CS and include the KB link in the customer-facing note?

If 5% for 24 hours + replay window is possible, we can proceed. Otherwise we’ll need to re-scope the initial ramp.

Regards —
Priya Mehta
Program Manager, Atlas Corp
pm@atlascorp.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <pm@atlascorp.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Feature-flag contingency & docs owners

All — agreed on 5% for 24 hours with the replay window. Updated plan below (finalized):

Launch cadence (final):
- Day 0: 5% canary (24h) + replay enabled; automated health checks (latency p95 / p99, error rate) + QA probe token-quality. Manual hold at 24h.
- Day 1: 25% (6h), monitor; if stable, proceed to 100% with a final manual go/no-go.

Rollback & abort rules:
- Auto-abort on latency p95 > 2x baseline OR error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5 minutes.
- Manual abort: triage by Platform (Ben), SRE, and Product (Marissa).

Owners: 
- Docs owner: Laura Bennett — operator runbook, customer KB snippet, and CS note. Laura: please add the doc links to the Drive folder and ping Priya when initial KB is available.
- Rollback scripts / ops runbook: Ben Carter (push to ops repo).
- Metric gating: Karthik Iyer (define exact signals + thresholds).

Attachments (pushed to Drive): uv_ready_checklist.xlsx, feature-flag-matrix.csv. Links: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/Launch/Runtime2-Contingency, JIRA SUP-5421.

If there are no objections by EOD today I’ll schedule the 5% canary for Monday 06/22 09:00 PDT.

Thanks —
Marissa
